body_markdown:
Building an app used to mean coordinating separate database hosting, authentication services, backend infrastructure, and deployment pipelines. Today, platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) bring these capabilities together, allowing users to build and publish full-stack applications through AI assistants without managing separate infrastructure services.


According to the 2026 Stack Overflow survey,[83% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data) reported using at least one AI tool in their work. This reflects the growing adoption of AI-assisted workflows. However, generating an interface is only one part of building a working application. Database integration, authentication, and hosting determine whether an app can store information and support users beyond an initial demonstration.


This guide covers 12 AI app builders with built-in database capabilities, examining their database architecture, AI generation features, production readiness, pricing, and suitability for different users. Pricing and product details reflect information available as of November 2026 for readers planning their 2027 projects.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Full-stack app development:**[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) allows supported AI assistants to create, edit, and publish applications while Floot provides managed databases, authentication, and hosting.
- **Persistent data matters:** Applications requiring customer accounts, orders, or saved records benefit from[managed database services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) that reduce infrastructure configuration.
- **Existing AI subscriptions:** Floot supports[assistant-based building](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , allowing eligible users to work through their existing AI subscriptions without separate Floot AI build-credit charges.
- **Ownership and portability:** Floot users own their project code and data, while[project exports](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) provide an option for moving code to another environment.
- **Consider ongoing costs:** Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with paid plans offering higher daily build-action allowances, monthly AI credits, and hosting allowances.


## **What to Look for in an AI App Builder with Built-In Hosting**


Choosing an AI app builder requires evaluating more than how quickly it generates an interface. A suitable platform should support persistent information, reliable authentication, deployment, and ongoing application maintenance. Database architecture, pricing, and ownership also affect how easily an application can grow.


- **Database architecture:** PostgreSQL supports structured relational data and SQL queries, making it suitable for customer records, transactions, and business applications. Firestore and other NoSQL databases use different data models. Some platforms offer proprietary databases with platform-specific management features.
- **Authentication integration:** User accounts should be protected through appropriate authentication and authorization. Built-in login services can reduce setup work, while OAuth providers allow supported external sign-in options. Floot includes[authentication services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) within its managed infrastructure.
- **Production readiness:** Evaluate database backups, hosting limits, application monitoring, custom domains, and scaling capabilities. A working prototype does not automatically establish production reliability. Testing and application architecture remain important.
- **AI generation quality:** Consider whether generated applications can be updated consistently, whether the platform supports debugging, and how well it handles changes to database schemas and backend logic.
- **Ownership and portability:** Verify who owns the application code and data, what export formats are available, and whether migration requires additional configuration. Code ownership does not necessarily mean that deployment elsewhere requires no changes.
- **Pricing structure:** Compare AI credits, build actions, hosting usage, database storage, and user-based fees. Platforms may charge for different activities, so a lower subscription price does not automatically mean lower overall operating costs.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


The connected AI assistant handles development tasks, while Floot provides managed infrastructure. Available building capabilities depend on the AI client's connector permissions and supported tools.


### **How Floot Builds Apps**


Floot allows users to describe application requirements in natural language through a supported AI assistant.


The connected assistant can work with Floot's tools to create projects, modify files, manage database operations, inspect logs, and publish applications. This approach lets users work within an existing AI environment instead of managing separate development services.


Floot is designed for non-technical founders, business owners, and operators who need functioning applications with saved data and user accounts.


### **Database and Backend Capabilities**


Floot provides managed PostgreSQL databases with SQL access and a browser-based data interface.


Its[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) include:


- Managed PostgreSQL databases and hosting
- User authentication and file storage
- Transactional email and external integrations
- Background jobs and scheduled tasks
- Custom domains and application publishing


These services support applications such as customer portals, booking systems, internal dashboards, and business management tools.


### **Authentication and Ownership**


Floot supports email/password authentication and built-in Google and Microsoft sign-in. Apple and other OAuth providers can also be configured using the app owner's registered OAuth credentials. Users retain ownership of their project code, data, and intellectual property.


Database exports are available through the platform, while full project code downloads are offered on paid plans. The[export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains how users can obtain their application files and database data. Running exported applications elsewhere may require additional infrastructure configuration.


### **Flexible Building Workflows**


Floot supports multiple development workflows through its MCP connector and[in-app editor](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/editor-and-preview) . Compatible assistants can work alongside Floot's managed infrastructure rather than being replaced by it.


Floot also supports mobile app workflows, converting web applications into iOS and Android builds through its managed cloud-building process. Users do not need to install Xcode or Android Studio locally. App-store publishing requires the relevant developer accounts and store approval.


### **Pricing**


[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) is free to start, with three published plans:


- **Free ($0/month):** 100 daily building actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year, and 2 mobile builds per month. Free has no recurring monthly hosting allowance.
- **Pro ($25/month):** 1,000 daily building actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. It also includes custom-domain features and priority support.
- **Power ($100/month):** 5,000 daily building actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds.


Building through connected AI assistants uses the user's eligible AI subscription rather than Floot AI build credits. Floot credits may apply to optional AI features, image generation, or building through Floot's own agent. Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-based.


As of November 16, 2026, Floot supports mobile app builds on every plan: 2 per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited on Power. Floot handles the builds without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio installations. Apple developer-account connections are supported on every Floot plan, while connecting Google Play requires a paid plan. App-store publishing requires the relevant developer accounts and store approval.


## **2. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications through ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites integrates conversational website creation with hosting and publishing. Users can build lightweight applications without setting up a separate deployment environment.


### **Key Features**


- Persistent database storage for supported applications
- Interactive websites and lightweight web apps
- Site-sharing and access controls
- Integration with connected applications and existing permissions


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites operates within a supported runtime. Applications requiring specific frameworks, custom backend configurations, or specialized infrastructure should be checked for compatibility. Site database storage and hosting are subject to platform limits.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available through eligible ChatGPT subscriptions, including Plus, Pro, and supported organizational plans. Building and editing count toward Codex usage. Hosting is included through December 2026, with usage-based charges above applicable allowances scheduled to begin in January 2027 for certain plans.


## **3. Replit**


Replit provides a cloud development environment with AI-assisted code generation, integrated databases, and deployment tools.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit combines an editor, terminal, package management, database services, and hosting in one development environment.


### **Key Features**


- Integrated PostgreSQL database support
- Replit Agent for AI-assisted development
- Cloud IDE with terminal access
- Collaborative development and deployment tools


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit offers a development environment suitable for users who want access to application code and technical configuration. Its Free plan supports limited published applications, while paid plans provide expanded development resources and usage allowances.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit Core costs $20/month or $18/month when billed annually. It is suitable for teams that want AI-assisted development alongside conventional coding tools. For additional context, see[Floot's Replit comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) .


## **4. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI app builder that generates web applications with React-based interfaces and integrated backend capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable focuses on conversational application generation and iterative visual editing.


### **Key Features**


- Supabase PostgreSQL integration
- Lovable Cloud backend services
- AI-generated interfaces with visual editing
- Authentication and application publishing


### **App Building Considerations**


The Free plan provides 5 daily build credits, capped at 30 per month. Users should evaluate credit consumption, hosting requirements, and backend configuration when developing applications that require repeated changes.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable Pro costs $25/month or approximately $21/month when billed annually, with 100 base monthly credits. The platform suits teams prioritizing conversational web development and interface customization. A separate[Floot comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) discusses differences in development workflows.


## **5. Taskade Genesis**


Taskade Genesis combines AI application generation with workspace-based data, AI agents, and automation workflows.


### **Primary Focus**


Taskade Genesis creates hosted applications connected to workspace projects, agents, and automations.


### **Key Features**


- Built-in workspace-based database
- AI agents with configurable capabilities
- Hosted application publishing
- Automation workflows with external integrations


### **App Building Considerations**


The Free plan supports up to 3 published applications, 1 AI agent, and 10 automation runs per month. AI-assisted generation depends on available credits, which can be earned on the Free plan or included with paid subscriptions.


### **Organizational Fit**


Taskade Starter costs $8/month or $6/month when billed annually. Taskade Pro starts at $20/month or $16/month annually, offering additional AI credits, agents, and automation capacity. Taskade Genesis fits teams that want applications connected to collaborative workspaces.


## **6. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new provides browser-based application development using StackBlitz WebContainers technology.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt combines natural-language application generation with a browser-based Node.js development environment.


### **Key Features**


- Unlimited databases on the Free plan
- Browser-based development through WebContainers
- Integrated hosting and deployment
- Up to 333,000 included web requests on Free hosting


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt's Free plan includes 1 million tokens per month, with a daily limit of 300,000 tokens. Users should consider token consumption and database requirements when building applications with complex backend functionality.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt Pro starts at $25/month with expanded token allowances and hosting features. Bolt is suitable for browser-based development workflows that combine AI assistance with a live coding environment. For a Floot-focused comparison, see[Floot vs Bolt](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **7. Softr**


Softr is a no-code platform for building business applications, client portals, and internal tools using native or connected data sources.


### **Primary Focus**


Softr combines visual application building with database connections and access-management features.


### **Key Features**


- Native Softr Database
- Connections to external data sources
- User authentication and permissions
- Published applications and client portals


### **App Building Considerations**


Softr's Free plan includes 5 app users and 5 monthly AI credits. The Basic plan includes 10 monthly AI credits. AI credit consumption depends on the feature and task. The platform focuses on client portals and database-backed business applications.


### **Organizational Fit**


Softr Basic costs $25/month or $19/month when billed annually. It is suitable for organizations building applications around existing business data.


## **8. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app-building platform owned by Wix that provides integrated application generation, databases, authentication, and hosting.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 enables users to generate applications through natural-language instructions without manually configuring database and deployment services.


### **Key Features**


- Built-in database and authentication
- AI-assisted application generation
- Integrated hosting
- Visual application editing


### **App Building Considerations**


The Free plan includes up to 5 applications, 25 monthly message credits, and 100 monthly integration credits. Paid plans expand available credits and application-management features.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 Starter costs $16/month when billed annually. The platform is designed for users who want prompt-based development with integrated backend services. See[Floot vs Base44](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) for additional workflow comparisons.


## **9. Zite**


Zite is an AI app builder featuring no-code databases, automation workflows, and visual application management.


### **Primary Focus**


Zite combines application creation with database storage and workflow automation.


### **Key Features**


- Built-in no-code database
- Visual workflow inspection
- Unlimited applications and users on Free
- Database records and workflow-run allowances


### **App Building Considerations**


The Free plan includes 5,000 database records and 1,000 workflow runs per month. Teams should evaluate record limits, available credits, and workflow allowances against expected application usage.


### **Organizational Fit**


Zite Pro costs $20/month when billed annually. It supports teams building database-backed applications with visual workflows and multiple users.


## **10. Retool**


Retool is a low-code platform for building internal applications with managed database services and external data connections.


### **Primary Focus**


Retool combines visual application development, database queries, workflows, and AI-assisted features for internal business tools.


### **Key Features**


- Managed Retool Database based on PostgreSQL
- External database connections
- Retool Agents and workflow automation
- SQL and graphical query interfaces


### **App Building Considerations**


Retool's Free plan supports up to 5 users, 500 monthly workflow runs, 250 pooled AI credits, and up to 20 monthly agent hours. Its managed database is intended for application data management, although workloads requiring high availability or specialized scaling may need separate database infrastructure.


### **Organizational Fit**


The Team plan costs $10 per builder/month and $5 per internal user/month when billed annually. Retool suits organizations creating internal tools that connect to operational data.


## **11. Google AI Studio**


Google AI Studio combines Gemini-powered app generation with supported Google Cloud and Firebase services.


### **Primary Focus**


Google AI Studio provides AI-assisted development connected to Google's cloud infrastructure and deployment services.


### **Key Features**


- Cloud Firestore database integration
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL support
- Firebase Authentication
- Google Cloud deployment capabilities


### **App Building Considerations**


Eligible Starter Tier users can build and deploy up to two applications using Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL within the provided quota. Additional applications may use Firestore or require different Google Cloud configurations. Database choice affects storage limits, data modeling, and billing.


### **Organizational Fit**


Google AI Studio offers a Starter Tier with limited no-cost resources for eligible accounts. Additional Google Cloud usage may require billing configuration and consumption-based charges. The platform suits teams working with Google Cloud and Firebase.


## **12. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual no-code application builder with a built-in database, workflow engine, and plugin ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble combines visual application design with database management and workflow automation.


### **Key Features**


- Built-in database with visual data management
- Visual workflow engine
- Plugin and API integrations
- AI-assisted application building


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble's Free plan supports application development and testing, with 50,000 workload units and 500 AI credits per month. Publishing a live application requires a paid plan. Production costs depend on workload usage, plan limits, and application requirements.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble's Web Starter plan costs $32/month when billed annually. Separate Mobile and Web & Mobile plans are available for applications requiring native mobile publishing. Bubble suits teams developing applications through visual workflows.


## **How Can Floot Help You Build and Publish a Full-Stack App?**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) helps founders, business owners, and operators develop database-backed applications without managing individual infrastructure services. Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , supported AI assistants can perform permitted development tasks while Floot supplies the services needed to run and publish the application.


Its infrastructure supports:


- **Persistent data:** Managed PostgreSQL databases for application records.
- **User accounts:** Built-in authentication and supported OAuth providers.
- **Hosting:** Application deployment with usage-based hosting allowances.
- **Backend services:** File storage, email, scheduled jobs, and integrations.
- **App ownership:** Code and data ownership, with paid project downloads.


Users can build through compatible AI assistants or use Floot's[in-app editor](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/editor-and-preview) . Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with paid plans providing higher building allowances and infrastructure capacity.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How do AI app builders with built-in databases differ from traditional development?**


Traditional development often involves configuring databases, authentication, backend services, and deployment separately. AI app builders can connect these components through an integrated workflow. For example,[Floot's infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) provides managed PostgreSQL, authentication, hosting, and related services, allowing supported AI assistants to work with those resources during application development.


### **Can users build apps with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or Cursor?**


Yes, when the assistant and its configuration support the required integration. Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development tasks while Floot manages infrastructure. Available operations depend on the client's connector permissions and capabilities.


### **What type of database does Floot provide?**


Floot provides managed PostgreSQL databases for storing structured application data. Users can inspect tables, run SQL queries, and export database content. The platform also offers authentication, file storage, and other backend services. Its[database and backend](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) capabilities support applications such as CRMs, booking systems, and client portals.


### **How much does it cost to build and host an app with Floot?**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) . Its Free plan includes 100 daily build actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year. Pro costs $25/month, while Power costs $100/month. Hosting usage beyond allowances can incur additional charges. Building through a supported connected AI assistant uses the user's existing eligible AI subscription rather than Floot AI build credits.


### **Who owns the code and data created with Floot?**


Users own their application code, data, and intellectual property. Database exports are available through the platform, while downloading complete project code is a paid-plan feature. The[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains these options. Running an exported application outside Floot may require additional hosting, database, and authentication configuration.
